method.introduction: Put a method born at Google to work for your team.
method.description: Jake Knapp started the Design Sprint at Google, and GV developed the method. Idea Boost draws on its approach.
method.scope: Idea Boost helps you decide on one idea. Prototyping and user testing come next.
method.cases: Google's Design Sprint Kit includes case studies from 3M × Bontouch, H&M, and Headspace.

principles.title: Start with a
principles.label: Find the problem
principles.description: Before proposing ideas, decide whose problem you want to solve and choose it together.
principles.evidence: Lack of market fit is one reason startups fail.

principles.title: Think alone,
principles.label: From individual work to sharing
principles.description: Everyone writes first, without waiting for a turn to speak. Private notes capture each person's thinking.
principles.evidence: In spoken brainstorming, waiting to speak can reduce the number of ideas generated.

principles.title: Choose without being swayed,
principles.label: Private voting
principles.description: Choose from your own perspective, without seeing others' votes while voting.
principles.evidence: Inspired by the silent voting used in Design Sprints.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: Teams that reached one idea took about two hours (median). Time varies with the number of people and the discussion. Each step has a timer to guide you.

items.question: Can I use it without knowing Design Sprints?
items.answer: Yes. A full Design Sprint takes five days, including prototyping and testing, with a facilitator leading the team. Idea Boost covers choosing one idea (usually the first three days) and guides you with step-by-step instructions and timers.

items.question: What do I need?
items.answer: A browser with an internet connection. You can start as a guest without a Google account by entering a name. This introduction page works on desktop and mobile. Full board functionality is not guaranteed on every smartphone.

items.question: How long are outcomes saved?
items.answer: People present at completion, and those who left after saving an outcome, can revisit it for 180 days after first completion. Incomplete shared outcomes are kept for 180 days after the last use. After that, they can no longer be viewed, so copy or save anything you want to keep. See “Storage and privacy” below.

items.question: Is this a Google product?
items.answer: No. Idea Boost is not a Google product and is not endorsed by or affiliated with Google. It draws on Design Sprint thinking.
